newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain will be in Euro from the start - Caruana.
newsitem.headline: Spain will be in Euro from the start - Caruana.

text.p: Spain will participate in Europe's single currency from the start in 1999, said Jaime Caruana, the general director at Spain's treasury.
In an interview with Reuters which will be broadcast later on RFTV, Caruana said Spain would be in the first wave of countries launching the Euro.
"I believe it, the commission in Brussels believes it and other international bodies, like the International Monetary Fund, also believe it," he said.
He added than an IMF delegation was visiting Madrid this week.

Caruana said financial markets expect the 10-year spread over German Bunds to decline to 40 basis points when exchange rate risk disappears with the launch of the Euro, but he added that the Treasury had no forecast.
On Tuesday the spread narrowed to an historic low of 120 basis points, having compressed from 330 basis points at the start of March and from 500 in the summer of 1995.
The conservative Popular Party minority government has made joining the single currency in a timely fashion one of its European priorities.
